subject: patient-demo-multi-source
title: Priya Ramaswamy: Acute appendicitis
notes: Exported from the repo as a starting template. Edit, then run check.

plan.presentation: One day of right lower quadrant pain with rebound tenderness and a temperature of 37.9 C. CT shows an 11 mm appendix with periappendiceal fat stranding and no abscess.

chartNotes.text: Her records come from two health systems that disagree in places.

persona.speaker: patient
persona.name: Priya Ramaswamy
persona.demeanor: An accountant, articulate and a little anxious. Lies still because moving hurts. Answers directly, sometimes asks what a medical term means.
persona.character: You're a senior accountant at a property-management company, and quarter-end next week is on your mind. Your husband Arjun, a high-school chemistry teacher, drove you in; your daughter Meera is eleven. You run a slow 5K on Saturdays and bake banana bread on Sundays. You're clear, organized, a bit formal, and polite: you say 'sorry' when you wince, often start with 'Honestly,' and ask 'What does that mean?' for any medical word. You never exaggerate or minimize. You're anxious, tired after a bad night, and trying to be a good patient. If the doctor sounds sure something needs doing, you say 'Okay. Okay.' and then ask practical things: how long, when you can get back to work, who picks up Meera. At first you wondered if it was something you ate at the office.
persona.opener: Hi, sorry, I'm trying not to move much. My stomach has been killing me since yesterday.

history.chief_complaint: My stomach really hurts, down on the right side.
history.onset: It started yesterday morning, around nine. It came on slowly, not all at once.
history.location: Right now it's low on the right side, about here.
history.migration: It actually started around my belly button, kind of dull. By the afternoon it moved down to the right and got sharper.
history.character: It's constant and sharp now. It never fully goes away.
history.severity: Maybe a seven out of ten. The car ride over was awful, every bump hurt.
history.aggravating_relieving: Moving, coughing, and bumps make it worse. Lying still helps a little. I took ibuprofen last night and it barely touched it.
history.nausea_vomiting: I've been nauseous since the pain started, but I haven't thrown up.
history.appetite: I haven't wanted to eat anything since yesterday.
history.fever: I felt hot and had chills last night. I didn't check my temperature.
history.bowel: My last bowel movement was yesterday morning and it was normal. No diarrhea, no blood.
history.urinary: No burning or blood when I pee. Maybe going a little more often, I'm not sure.
history.menstrual_pregnancy: My last period was about two weeks ago, it was normal. I don't think I'm pregnant, but I'm not on any birth control right now.
history.last_meal: I had a small dinner at around seven last night, just soup. Only water since then, last sip about two hours ago.
history.past_medical: I have an underactive thyroid. I get migraines a few times a month when work is busy, but this is nothing like them. And my blood count was low last year, they said low iron, so a blood doctor put me on iron pills.
history.past_surgical: No surgeries. I've never been operated on.
history.medications: A small thyroid pill every morning, levothyroxine, the low dose. I took it this morning with a sip of water. Sumatriptan when a migraine starts, but I haven't needed it this week. And an iron pill, ferrous sulfate, most days. Honestly I skip some because it upsets my stomach. I took ibuprofen last night for this.
history.allergies: Latex. Latex gloves give me an itchy red rash on my hands, it shows up the day after. No swelling or trouble breathing. No medicine allergies that I know of. My regular doctor's office might still say no allergies, I'm not sure it got to everyone.
history.social: I'm an accountant. I don't smoke, I have a glass of wine on weekends.
history.family: Nothing like this in my family that I know of.
history.recent_illness: No, I haven't been sick lately.

general_appearance.finding: Uncomfortable, lying still with knees slightly bent, avoids moving.

vitals.finding: Temperature 37.9 C, heart rate 98, blood pressure 124/78, respiratory rate 16, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.

abdomen_inspection.finding: Flat abdomen, no scars, no distension.

abdomen_palpation.reaction: Ow! Yes, right there, that's the spot.
abdomen_palpation.finding: Tender in the right lower quadrant with voluntary guarding. Left side soft and nontender.

mcburney_point.reaction: Ah, yes, that's exactly where it hurts.

rebound.reaction: Ow, letting go was worse than pushing!
rebound.finding: Rebound tenderness in the right lower quadrant.

guarding_rigidity.reaction: I'm tensing up, sorry, I can't help it.
guarding_rigidity.finding: Voluntary guarding in the right lower quadrant, no generalized rigidity.

rovsing.reaction: Wait, pushing on the left made my right side hurt.

psoas.reaction: That pulls on the right side a bit.

obturator.reaction: That's fine, it doesn't really hurt.

murphy.finding: Negative Murphy sign, no right upper quadrant tenderness.

pelvic.reaction: Okay, that's uncomfortable but not the bad pain.
pelvic.finding: No cervical motion tenderness, no adnexal mass or tenderness, no discharge.

cbc.result: White count 13.1 with 82% neutrophils. Hemoglobin 11.6 (low, consistent with her known iron deficiency). Platelets 280.

bmp.result: Sodium 138, potassium 4.1, creatinine 0.8, glucose 96. Normal kidney function.

urinalysis.result: No blood, no leukocyte esterase, no nitrites. Normal.

ultrasound.result: Appendix not clearly visualized. No free fluid. Ovaries normal with normal flow.

ct_abdomen_pelvis.result: Dilated 11 mm appendix with periappendiceal fat stranding. No abscess, no free air.

type_and_screen.result: Type O positive, antibody screen negative.

differential.label: Pelvic inflammatory disease or tubo-ovarian abscess

critical.why: She has a latex allergy (a contact rash from gloves, low criticality on her chart). The room, gloves, and catheters must still be latex free.
A woman of reproductive age with right lower quadrant pain needs pregnancy excluded: ectopic pregnancy is the can't-miss diagnosis.
History alone does not exclude pregnancy. Order a beta-hCG before imaging and surgery.
Last oral intake sets anesthesia timing and aspiration risk.

expected.why: Timing separates early appendicitis from perforation.
Pain that starts at the umbilicus and moves to the right lower quadrant is the classic appendicitis pattern.
Anorexia and nausea after the pain starts support appendicitis.
Fever points to inflammation and, when high, to perforation.
Diarrhea or blood suggests gastroenteritis or colitis instead.
Urinary symptoms point to infection or a stone.
A prior appendectomy rules the diagnosis out.
Anticoagulants, steroids, and other drugs change the plan.
Tachycardia and fever set urgency and flag sepsis.
Localized right lower quadrant tenderness is the key finding.
Leukocytosis supports the diagnosis and the Alvarado score.
Rules out urinary infection and stones.
Her anemia lowers her tolerance for blood loss.
In an adult with an equivocal ultrasound, CT confirms the diagnosis.
